answer: To enter, an applicant escrows a one-use cipher as four deposit shards with custodians who have never co-signed that key family, drawn from a published nebula roster. Each custodian releases its shard only after a distinct live work-proof, unique in this epoch, is bound to the shard hash. Settlement then forms an anchor from the custodian-host set, key-family prefix, and proof-interval skeleton; any two applicants sharing that anchor have both escrows slashed and those custodians benched two epochs, so cloned identities cannot cheaply reuse the same host and timing path.
